summary: Isaac G. Strain, a lieutenant of the United States Navy, arrived at Valparaiso from San Francisco in February 1849 and made a journey overland to the Atlantic. He rode to Santiago, crossed the Andes to Mendoza, and galloped across the pampas by San Luis and Rio Quarto to Buenos Ayres.

Several chapters describe Valparaíso and Santiago and set out the early history of Chile, its revolution, and its government; from the crossing of the Cordillera onward the book is a journal of the ride, with the post-houses, the gauchos, and the politics of Rosas’s Argentina. It has many footnotes and no illustrations.
